summary.text: Chris Pappas is the Democratic nominee for the open New Hampshire U.S. Senate seat. A Manchester native who co-owns his family's restaurant, he served in the state House, as Hillsborough County treasurer and on the Executive Council before winning New Hampshire's 1st District U.S. House seat in 2018. He announced his Senate campaign in April 2025 after Sen. Jeanne Shaheen said she would not seek re-election.

paragraphs.text: Born in Manchester, New Hampshire, in 1980; graduated from Manchester Central High School in 1998. His great-grandfather founded what is now the family-owned Puritan Backroom restaurant in Manchester.
Earned a bachelor's degree in government from Harvard in 2002.
Is a co-owner of his family's restaurant, the Puritan Backroom; his House website describes him as a lifelong Manchester resident and small business owner.
Volunteered on Jeanne Shaheen's 1996 gubernatorial campaign as a high school student. Elected to the New Hampshire House of Representatives in 2002 and served two terms.

Served as treasurer of Hillsborough County from 2007 to 2011 (he lost a 2010 re-election bid to Bob Burns), then won the Executive Council seat for District 4 in 2012 by defeating Burns, serving until 2019.

Won the Democratic primary for New Hampshire's 1st Congressional District in 2018 and has represented the district in the U.S. House since; he was the first openly gay U.S. House member elected from New Hampshire.
In the House he serves on the Transportation and Infrastructure and Veterans' Affairs committees, and is co-chair of the Congressional Equality Caucus.
Announced his Senate candidacy on April 3, 2025, and won the September 8, 2026 Democratic primary with 64.6% of the vote over Karishma Manzur (33.2%).
